analysis.title: Rates Spark: Treasuries with blinkers on
key_insights: Treasuries ignored a solid post-midterm Conference Board consumer confidence report, with the overall index back above 100 for the first time since early 2025.
Treasuries also shrugged off the Monday Nvidia reversal, with yields moving lower rather than higher.
Bearish derivatives positioning in Treasuries has increased, but not enough to sway the market yet.
ING expects Wednesday's PCE report to be hot, with core PCE at 3.2% YoY as the central market expectation and headline at 3.8% YoY. Confirmation is seen as enough to abort the downtrend in yields.
Lower energy prices help headline inflation but feed through to core more slowly, for example airfares.
Eurozone rates are dragged along by souring US equity sentiment. The 10y Bund yield is just above 3.25%, near the early November low.
Reported US tariffs on China, the EU and other partners add to the equity gloom, and oil prices staying contained supports lower rates.
Eurozone natural gas prices are creeping higher in a cold spell, tempering the benefit of lower oil.
Wednesday's calendar includes PCE at 0.3% MoM consensus, second Q3 GDP estimate, durable goods, jobless claims and the Beige Book. ING says 0.3% is too hot for the Fed and keeps a hawkish bias.
The ECB Governing Council meets non-policy to discuss a higher minimum reserve requirement, with a decision possibly delayed to December or February.
Auctions: Italy €3.5bn short BTP and linkers, Germany €5bn 10y Bunds, US $44bn new 7y notes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Central market expectation, ING sees confirmation as enough to halt the Treasury yield downtrend.
Headline is expected to remain high even as energy prices ease.
Consensus level seen as too hot for the Fed, keeps a hawkish bias.
First time above 100 since early 2025, about a 10-point rise across all three key indices, ignored by bonds.
Close to early November low, supported by equity gloom.

risk_factors: A hot PCE print could end the Treasury yield downtrend.
Renewed tariff announcements could weigh on equity sentiment and growth.
Higher eurozone gas prices from the cold spell could temper the benefit of lower oil.
Core inflation is slow to respond to lower energy prices.
vol_and_positioning: Bearish positions in Treasury derivatives have increased behind the scenes, but not enough to move the overall market yet.
geopolitical: US government reportedly close to announcing tariffs on China, the EU and other trading partners.

tension_points.bull_case: Treasuries keep ignoring strong consumer data and the Nvidia reversal, with equity gloom and contained oil supporting lower yields.
tension_points.bear_case: PCE at 3.2% core and 3.8% headline is too hot for the Fed, and bearish derivatives positioning is building.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Confirmation of the expected PCE print on Wednesday, which ING thinks is enough to abort the yield downtrend.

theme_stances.evidence: confirmation will, in fact, be enough to abort the downtrend in yields
